title: The Borrowed Compass
premise: In 1871 Marseille, Odile Delacroix, a quietly brilliant apprentice clockmaker hiding a forged identity, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds an abandoned child at its door, along with a note ordering him to forget the face. The child is the illegitimate heir of the observatory's dying director, and the director's powerful family intends to erase her from every record. As Odile repairs the clock that governs the city's official time, he races to document the truth before the family's historians seal the archives, finding unexpected allies among the observatory's outcasts who become his first real family. In the end, Odile sacrifices his own anonymity—testifying under his true name at a probate hearing—to secure the child's inheritance, choosing love and truth over the invisibility that once kept him safe.
about_author: Marguerite Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing contested wills in provincial French records offices. She writes historical fiction about the people history tried to leave out.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Hold
chapters.summary: Odile Delacroix arrives at the Marseille observatory to repair its failing master clock, keeping his head down as always. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: wary competence—the comfort of being needed only for one's hands.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: During a storm, Odile finds a small girl abandoned at the observatory door with a note: 'Forget this face.' He cannot bring himself to turn her away. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking his careful anonymity.

chapters.title: The Director's Last Windings
chapters.summary: Odile learns the girl resembles the dying Director Aubertin, whose estranged family controls the estate. The director, lucid for one hour, begs Odile to remember what the records must show. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: dawning responsibility.

chapters.title: People of the Margins
chapters.summary: Odile gathers unlikely allies: the night astronomer dismissed for her sex, a deaf archivist's assistant, and the observatory cook. Together they hide the child, whom they name Céleste. POV: rotating between allies. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared risk.

chapters.title: The Family Historian
chapters.summary: The Aubertin heir apparent, Gaspard, arrives with a hired historian to compile a flattering family record—and begins asking about a missing child. Odile plays the invisible workman while memorizing everything. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Clock Remembers
chapters.summary: Inside the master clock's casing, Odile discovers the director's hidden letters acknowledging Céleste as his daughter. The mechanism itself becomes the vault of truth. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: hope entangled with fear of discovery.

chapters.title: Betrayal by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Gaspard raids the observatory; the letters are seized and the cook dismissed for harboring the child. Céleste barely escapes through the dome. POV: the night astronomer. Emotional beat: grief and fury at how power rewrites rooms it enters.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: With the archive sealing in three days, the allies plan to restore the seized evidence by proving the historian's record contains forged dates—verifiable against the very clock Odile repaired. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: The Testimony of Small Hours
chapters.summary: At the probate hearing, Odile abandons his false identity and testifies under his true name, presenting the clock's escapement log as proof of tampering. Gaspard's forgery unravels. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: Setting the Hands Right
chapters.summary: Céleste is recognized as heir; the found family keeps the observatory together, and Odile, no longer hiding, winds the master clock himself as dawn breaks over Marseille. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging—time finally on their side.
